::: {.hero-panel}
This page is the submission hub for the Option B study of road traffic accidents in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region during 2022. The technical report completes the six required tasks and a value-added space-time analysis.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Main result"}
The final pattern contains **3,597 distinct recorded accidents**. Broad concentration centres on Bangkok and extends towards Samut Prakan. An inhomogeneous L-function test still finds excess neighbouring events after the broad intensity trend is controlled, while the bonus Knox test finds more space-time-close pairs than expected under time permutation.
:::

## Brief at a glance

The [official exercise brief](https://isss626-ay2026-27aug.netlify.app/take-home_ex01) requires six connected tasks:

1. Acquire, inspect, clean, validate, transform, and document the spatial data.
2. Analyse first-order spatial and temporal intensity with justified parameters.
3. Test second-order spatial structure against a stated null model.
4. Integrate the first- and second-order evidence, including uncertainty and alternative explanations.
5. Present readable statistical graphics and maps, with no more than 150 words for each major visualisation.
6. Write public-safety implications in no more than 500 words, separating evidence from recommendations that need more information.

The bonus analysis must answer a useful geospatial question beyond the core requirements. A new package or decorative visualisation alone does not meet the bonus standard.

## Selected study design

The analysis uses **Option B: Thailand road accidents in 2022**. The event file is the actual [Thailand Road Accident 2019-2022 dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thaweewatboy/thailand-road-accident-2019-2022), and the study boundary is the actual [geoBoundaries Thailand ADM1 dataset](https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/THA/ADM1/).

The Bangkok Metropolitan Region is operationalised as Bangkok, Samut Prakan, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Pathom, and Samut Sakhon. This six-province definition is documented by Thailand's National Statistical Office. Distance and area calculations use WGS 84 / UTM zone 47N (EPSG:32647).

The private repository note [`_OPTION_COMPARISON.md`](https://github.com/davincuaso/ISSS608-VAA/blob/master/Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex01/_OPTION_COMPARISON.md) records the comparison of Options A and B. It is planning material, not part of the assessed findings.

## Analytical coverage

- **Data quality:** 81,735 raw records were audited; 21,032 occurred in 2022; 189 lacked coordinates; spatial filtering and duplicate handling produced 3,597 events.
- **First order:** daily monthly intensity, hourly distribution, province event density and edge-corrected KDE at 2 km, 3 km and 6 km bandwidths.
- **Second order:** transformed L-functions under CSR and an inhomogeneous Poisson model, each using 99 conditional simulations and translation edge correction.
- **Robustness:** common-scale bandwidth comparison and event-level intensity rank correlations.
- **Bonus:** a 199-run Monte Carlo Knox test at three space-time thresholds.
- **Reproducibility:** fixed data URLs, checksums, processing scripts, parameter documentation, a fixed random seed and session information.

## Deadline and delivery

The brief gives a deadline of **27 September 2026 at 11:59 pm**. Submit the Vercel links for the executive summary and technical report together with the GitHub repository link through the course channels described in the brief.
